title: His second marriage to Mazie and women on the road
summary: He married Mazie, a West Indian woman, in 1957, she left him, and he boasts of a girl in every town.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. You married again, didn't you?

Yeah, I married in '57. And the girl would always say, 'I'm going home to Ma,' when I'd be out and she'd want me to stay. I'd say, 'I can't make no money home.' So one day I came back and she sure was gone.
She was a West Indian girl, pretty girl.
Well, you always had pretty women because you're a sharp dude, man. Lord knows, you had your share. You ain't missed a thing, Tom.
Hey, I stop and think about all the girls I -- I was a terror, I must have been.
You were, man, I saw you. Remember me?
I had a girl in every town.
